ov: Six species of alligator relatives from Central and South America, living in marshes, swamps, lakes and mangrove rivers and fairly nocturnal. Most are small crocodilians of 6–40 kg, but the black caiman of the Amazon basin can top 4 m and 450 kg.

why.et: Humans are their main predator, hunting caimans for their meat and skin.
why.dg: Potentially dangerous to people and pets, though smaller than other crocodilians and so less of a threat.
why.ac: It usually hunts at night, and has excellent night vision.

len: Most 2–2.5 m; black caiman over 4 m
wt: Mostly 6–40 kg; black caiman over 450 kg
rg: Central and South America; the spectacled caiman has been introduced to Florida, Cuba and Puerto Rico.
df: Mainly fish, plus insects, birds, small mammals and reptiles.
fx: In droughts, caimans may dig a burrow and wait it out in a summer dormancy called aestivation.
About four million spectacled caimans live in Venezuela alone.
